title: The Year Merrill Fernando Finally Put Dilmah on the Packet
conflicts: Money behind the launch: Fernando in 2014 said he 'started with very little money' and stood to lose everything (Lucire), while Ellis (2007) and the Sunday Times (2013) say Soviet bulk-tea earnings paid for it; the story gives his words and the earlier reports side by side. London training dated 1950s variously (1952, about 1954, 1956); story says 'the mid-1950s'. First Coles business: own-label deal in the mid-1980s (WIPO) vs two Dilmah-branded teas accepted in 1988 (STIR); told in sequence. Founding year sometimes given as 1985 or 1974; brand launch 1988 used.
notes: Stance is 'complicates': Okakura's 'no single recipe' sits against Fernando's conviction that only unblended tea was honest. Company field reads 'Dilmah (MJF Group)'.
